sanskrit: mokṣejāṃs todāṃs tumalān pathiṣṭhām̐ uta pārṣatān | ahīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣam arasaṃ kṛṇv oṣadhe ||
english: The mokṣeja, the toda, the tumala, those that dwell on the road, and the spotted ones — O herb, render powerless the venom of all these serpents.

sanskrit: aśvakrandasya vaṇḍasya pṛdākor gonaser uta | śvitrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣam arasaṃ kṛṇv oṣadhe ||
english: Of the aśvakranda, the vaṇḍa, the pṛdāku, and the gonasa — O herb, render powerless the venom of all the white-patched ones as well.

sanskrit: dyāṃpātasya gavakasya godhāpṛṣṭher aher uta | asitānām etaj jātam ariṣṭe 'rasaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Of the dyāṃpāta, the gavaka, and the snake with the godhā-striped back — make this whole breed of the black ones harmless; grant us freedom from harm.

sanskrit: etaj jātaṃ svajānāṃ tad babhro arasaṃ kṛdhi | sarvasya babhror bheṣajy asīha viṣadūṣaṇī ||
english: This breed of the svaja serpents — make that of the brown ones powerless. You are the remedy for every brown serpent here; you are the corrupter of venom.

sanskrit: trāyamāṇā pra bravītu sarvāṅ rājño ahīnām | tiraścirājīn asitān atho upaśayāś ca ye ||
english: Let the trāyamāṇā herb speak out against all the kings among serpents — the tiraścirājin, the black ones, and those that lie in ambush.

sanskrit: sahasāhaṃ yātudhānān sahasā yātudhānyaḥ | saho vaḥ sarvān sāsāha tasyāhaṃ nāma jagrabha ||
english: With might she overpowers the sorcerers; with might, the sorceresses. The power that has overpowered all of you — I have seized hold of its name.

sanskrit: sahaḥ sākaṃ paidvena- -ugreṇa vacasā mama | andhāhīṃś ca sṛjayāś ca śaphakāṃś ca rathavrayaḥ | sahasā saha utpatya tān sarvām̐ arasām̐ akaḥ ||
english: Together with Paidva's power and with my fierce utterance — the blind serpents, the sṛjaya snakes, the śaphaka, and the rathavra: leaping upon all of them together with force, she has made them all devoid of venom.

sanskrit: asitasya vidradhasya harito yaś ca vidradhaḥ | nimaṅkṣī vidradhānāṃ yo mṛjantī tām̐ ajījabhat ||
english: The yellow one that is a vidradha of the asita serpent, and whatever else is a vidradha — she who is the submerger of the vidradhas, the purifier: she crushed them all.

sanskrit: yaḥ svajānāṃ nīlagrīvo yaḥ svajānāṃ harir uta | kalmāṣapuccham oṣadhe jambhayāsy arundhati ||
english: The blue-throated one among the svajas, the tawny one among the svajas as well — O herb Arundhati, you crush the speckle-tailed one.

sanskrit: māyaṃ marad ahidaṣṭaḥ pitur asmā asad viṣam | imā hy asmā oṣadhim ā harāmy arundhatīm ||
english: Let not this man bitten by the serpent die; may his father's venom not be his. For I am bringing him this herb, Arundhati.

sanskrit: etaj jātaṃ pṛdākūnām arasaṃ jīvale kṛdhi | indrasya bhadrikā vīrud asīha viṣadūṣaṇī ||
english: This whole breed of the pṛdāku serpents — render it powerless, O jīvala. You are Indra's dear plant; you are here the corrupter of venom.

sanskrit: śatam arvāk pra syandante pra syandante śataṃ paraḥ | śataṃ vṛtrasya kāṇḍāni tebhya āpo vi dhāvatha ||
english: A hundred flow hither, a hundred flow yonder; a hundred are the shafts of Vṛtra. From those — O waters, flow apart and away.

sanskrit: antarikṣe patayiṣṇavo nabhasas pari jajñire | āpo hiraṇyavarṇās tās te bhavantu śaṃ hṛde ||
english: Fluttering through the mid-space, they were born forth from the cloud. Golden-hued are those waters — may they be beneficent to your heart.

sanskrit: śaṃ te santu hṛdayāya śaṃ te hṛdayyābhyaḥ | śaṃ te yakaklomabhyaḥ śam u te antaṣṭebhyaḥ ||
english: Benign be they to your heart; benign to the regions of your heart; benign to your liver and lungs; and benign also to your inner parts.

sanskrit: yad aṅgair apasismiṣe yac chīrṣṇā yac ca pṛṣṭibhiḥ | āpas tat sarvaṃ niṣ karan taṣṭā riṣṭam ivānasaḥ ||
english: Whatever you have trembled with in your limbs, whatever in the head, whatever in the joints of the back — may the waters cleanse all of that away, as a craftsman planes the broken part of a cart.

sanskrit: saṃ hṛdayena hṛdayam opaśena sam opaśaḥ | adbhir muñcāpasmitaṃ pārṣṇidyotaḥ sam etu me ||
english: Let heart be joined with heart, let the lobes of the lung be joined with the lobes. Release the seized limb with the waters; may the radiance of my heel come together whole.

sanskrit: ācarantīḥ parvatebhyo devīr devebhyas pari | āpo yam adya prāpan na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ ||
english: The divine waters coming down from the mountains, flowing forth from the gods — whatever man they reach today, that man shall suffer no harm.

sanskrit: śaṃ ta āpo haimavatīḥ śam u te santūtsyāḥ | śaṃ te saniṣyadā āpaḥ śam u te santu varṣyāḥ ||
english: Beneficent to you be the Himāvat waters; beneficent too be the spring-fed waters. Beneficent to you be the ever-flowing waters; and beneficent too be the rain-waters.

sanskrit: śaṃ ta āpo dhanvanyāḥ śam u te santv anūpyāḥ | śaṃ te khanitrimā āpaḥ śaṃ yāḥ kumbhebhir ābhṛtāḥ ||
english: Beneficent to you be the desert waters; beneficent too be the marshy waters. Beneficent to you be the well-dug waters; and those brought in jars — may they too be beneficent.

sanskrit: anabhrayaḥ khanamānā viprā gambhīre 'pasaḥ | bhiṣagbhyo bhiṣaktarā āpo acchā vadāmasi ||
english: Cloudless, digging their own way, inspired, deep in their flowing — more healing than healers: thus do we address the waters directly.

sanskrit: apām aha divyānām apāṃ srotasyānām | apām aha praṇejane 'śvā bhavatha vājinaḥ ||
english: By the divine waters, by the stream-flowing waters — by the waters that cleanse: O horses, become strong and swift!

sanskrit: tā āpaḥ śivā āpo 'yakṣmaṃkaraṇīr apaḥ | yathaiva tṛṣyate mayas tās ta ādyuttabheṣajī ||
english: Those waters are auspicious waters — waters that make one free of disease. Just as there is refreshment when one thirsts, so too are those waters the foremost remedy for you.

sanskrit: brahmajyeṣṭhā saṃbhṛtā vīryāṇi brahmāgre jyeṣṭhaṃ divam ā tatāna | bhūtānāṃ brahma prathamota jajñe tenārhati brahmaṇā spardhituṃ kaḥ ||
english: The powers gathered together have brahman as their chief; brahman in the beginning stretched out the highest heaven. Among all beings brahman was born first — who then is worthy to contend against brahman?

sanskrit: brahmeme dyāvāpṛthivī brahmeme sapta sindhavaḥ | brahmeme sarva ādityā brahma devā upāsate ||
english: These heaven and earth are brahman; these seven rivers are brahman; all these Ādityas are brahman; the gods attend upon brahman.

sanskrit: brahma brāhmaṇo vadati brahma rātrī ni viśate | sāvitraṃ brahmaṇo jātaṃ brahmaṇāgnir vi rocate ||
english: The brahmaṇa speaks brahman; into brahman the night retreats. That which belongs to Sāvitr̥ is born of brahman; through brahman Agni shines forth.

sanskrit: brahmauṣadhayo ni tiṣṭhanti brahma varṣanti vṛṣṭayaḥ | brahmedaṃ sarvam ātmanvad yāvat sūryo vipaśyati ||
english: The plants come to rest in brahman; the rains rain down as brahman. All this that is endowed with self — as far as the sun surveys it — that is brahman.

sanskrit: brahma hotā brahma yajño brahmaṇā svaravo mitāḥ | adhvaryur brahmaṇo jāto brahmaṇot tirate haviḥ ||
english: The hotr̥ priest is brahman, the sacrifice is brahman; the oblation-sticks are measured by brahman. The adhvaryu is born of brahman; through brahman the oblation is poured out.

sanskrit: brahma sruco ghṛtavatīr brahmaṇā vedir udyatā | brahma yajñasya tantava ṛtvijo ye haviṣkṛtaḥ ||
english: The ladling-spoons laden with ghee are brahman; the altar is raised up through brahman. The threads of the sacrifice are brahman — the officiating priests who have prepared the oblation.

sanskrit: brahma ṛṣabho bhadraretā brahma gāvo haviṣkṛtaḥ | brahma rathasya devasya yaj jayāti svaraṅkṛtaḥ ||
english: The bull of auspicious seed is brahman; the cows that produce the oblation are brahman. That chariot of the divine one which conquers while adorned with its own sound — it too is brahman.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā śīraṃ vahati brahmaṇā yujyate rathaḥ | brahmaṇā puruṣo dvipān na vyathate caran ||
english: Through brahman the plow is drawn; through brahman the chariot is yoked. Through brahman the two-footed man does not falter as he walks.

sanskrit: brahmaṇo jātā ṛṣayo brahmaṇo rājanyā uta | brahmedaṃ brahmaṇo jātaṃ brahmaṇo +'viṣyā annam ||
english: The seers were born of brahman; the royal warriors too are of brahman. This universe is brahman; all that is born is of brahman; the food that will be revealed is of brahman.

sanskrit: brahma śūdrā rājanyānāṃ brahmaiṣām uta vikṣadaḥ | brahmaiṣāṃ bhadraṃ sādanaṃ brahmaṇaiṣāṃ sabhāsadaḥ ||
english: The śūdras who serve the royal warriors are brahman; brahman also are those who tax them. Their auspicious dwelling-place is brahman; through brahman are their assembly-sitters.

sanskrit: brahma dāśā brahma dāsā brahmeme kitavā uta | strīpuṃsau brahmaṇo jātau striyo brahma uta vāvana ||
english: The fishermen are brahman, the slaves are brahman; these gamblers too are brahman. Woman and man, both born of brahman; women are brahman, and the weavers as well.

sanskrit: brahmodvato nivato brahma saṃvato vānaspatyāḥ parvatā brahma vīrudhaḥ | brahmedaṃ sarvam anv ā tatāna- -antarā dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe ||
english: Brahman on the heights, brahman in the valleys; brahman in the enclosed spaces — the forest trees, the mountains are brahman, the plants are brahman. Brahman has stretched out through all this, between both heaven and earth.

sanskrit: brahmaivābhūd uttaraṃ jātavedo radvajro yātudhānaṃ mahālam | bhavāśarvau tapuṣīṃ hetim asmai mayeṣitau vi sṛjatāṃ vadhāya ||
english: Brahman alone became the highest, O Jātaveda; the thunderbolt-wielder shattered the great demon sorcerer. May Bhava and Śarva, dispatched by Māyā, release their fiery weapon against him for his destruction.
